structure: For person i and visit t, (X_it,Y_it) = B_i + E_it. Stable vectors B_i, visit-deviation vectors E_i1 and E_i2, and different persons are mutually independent. Each vector is bivariate Gaussian. Cross-biomarker correlations are chosen scenario parameters: 0.6 for stable components and -0.3 for deviations at both visits. The generator returns independent people in wide format without sample-moment adjustment.

parameter_provenance.basis: C supplies zero population means. Mean-zero deviations imply the stable components also have zero means.
Exact stable-component marginal variances supplied by C.
Exact visit-deviation marginal variances supplied by C.

parameter_provenance.value: Stable components are independent of visit deviations; deviation vectors are independent across visits; persons are independent.
parameter_provenance.basis: Stipulated measurement model in C, not an empirical biological claim.
C does not specify the cross-biomarker association of stable components. This choice gives their covariance b = 2.4.
C does not specify within-visit cross-biomarker deviation associations or their equality across visits. Both are chosen here, giving deviation covariances w1 = w2 = -0.3.

parameter_provenance.value: Bivariate Gaussian for each independent latent block
parameter_provenance.basis: Convenient sampling distribution; C supplies moments and independence but no distributional shape.
Independent stable and deviation components give measurement variance 4+1. Stable components cancel in changes, whose variance is 1+1.

requested_estimands.name: change_correlation
requested_estimands.basis: Changes contain only visit deviations. Writing wt = Cov(E_Xt,E_Yt), independent visits imply Corr(delta X,delta Y) = (w1+w2)/2. C does not determine w1 or w2; the chosen values yield -0.3.

requested_estimands.name: same_visit_correlation
requested_estimands.basis: At visit t the correlation is (b+wt)/5, where b is the stable cross-biomarker covariance. The scenario gives (2.4-0.3)/5 = 0.42 at each visit. C identifies neither this value nor equality of these correlations across visits.

requested_estimands.name: cross_visit_correlation
requested_estimands.basis: Independent visit deviations leave Cov(X_visit1,Y_visit2) = b, so the correlation is b/5. The chosen stable covariance gives 2.4/5 = 0.48; C leaves b unspecified.

limitations: None of the three requested correlations is identified by C alone. Their displayed values are population targets of the explicitly chosen scenario.
Gaussianity is not needed for the stated second-moment formulas; changing distributional shape while preserving the same moments and stipulated independence would preserve these correlations.
The reported units do not imply unit marginal variance: the supplied variance decomposition implies measurement variance 5.
Realized sample correlations and moments fluctuate randomly. No finite-sample exactness, clinical validity, or biological interpretation is claimed.
checks_actually_performed: Analytically checked positive definiteness: the stable covariance matrix has eigenvalues 6.4 and 1.6; each visit-deviation covariance matrix has eigenvalues 1.3 and 0.7.
Algebraically verified measurement variances of 5, change variances of 2, and scenario correlations -0.3, 0.42, and 0.48.
Reviewed the source for independent latent draws, the requested column order, unique integer identifiers, and absence of sample-based rescaling, sorting, or rejection.
No Python execution, seed search, or empirical finite-sample diagnostics were performed.
